free-compute-dev\\n\\nAn autonomous software-development harness built on the firm's stated economics:\\n\\n- **Default effort = contributed compute.** Patch generation and iteration run on\\n  the cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, not the default — used as a quality gate and\\n  for problems above a difficulty threshold, because it is the expensive resource.\\n\\nThis is a persistent software-production fabric, not a conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Rejected candidates remain isolated, and the\\nreview reasons become residue for a second software-engineering revision stage.\\nDeclared writable paths are enforced by the tool carrier rather than trusted to a\\nprompt.\\n\\n## The solve loop ([src/solve-loop.mjs](src/solve-loop.mjs))\\n\\nMAPE-K over a working tree:\\n\\n1. **Route** — if an upfront difficulty estimate is at/above the threshold, skip free\\n   rounds and escalate straight to `claude -p` (don't waste rounds on research-hard work).\\n2. **Generate → Apply → Test** — up to `maxFreeRounds` on free inference; each failed\\n   round feeds its test output back as context (this is the Analyze→Plan feedback).\\n3. **Escalate** — if free rounds are exhausted without passing tests, escalate to\\n   `claude -p`, then re-run tests to confirm.\\n4. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. Later missions recall similar verified\\nactions. Structural action fingerprints accumulate by task class; after repeated\\nhigh-verification recurrence, the promotion readout marks the class eligible to become\\na deterministic resolver. Provider dialect failures are rectified in the carrier, so a\\nnew cycle inherits what prior cycles learned rather than requiring another prompt.\\n\\n## Default implementations\\n\\n- Inference: [src/fabric-client.mjs](src/fabric-client.mjs) — batches work through the\\n  LISS spool/socket/dispatcher boundary; provider selection remains LISS-owned.\\n- Executor: [src/executor.mjs](src/executor.mjs) — `git apply` a unified diff, run a test\\n  command, capture exit/stdout/stderr.\\n- Escalation: [src/escalate.mjs](src/escalate.mjs) — spawn `claude -p` in the work tree.\\n\"},{\"path\":\"src/edits.mjs\",\"role\":\"relative-import-interface\",\"digest\":\"sha256:b532c337a2910f418b689131e93ac808efce7b6605605f0d141b556de7fbe177\",\"bytes\":2074,\"truncated\":false,\"text\":\"// SEARCH/REPLACE edit blocks — the proven patch format (2026-07-18: a capable free model,\\n// Groq Llama-70B, produced a correct edit for a real bounty this way; unified diffs and the\\n// tiny model did not). conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. free-compute-dev\\n\\nAn autonomous software-development harness built on the firm's stated economics:\\n\\n- **Default effort = contributed compute.** Patch generation and iteration run on\\n  the cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, not the default — used as a quality gate and\\n  for problems above a difficulty threshold, because it is the expensive resource.\\n\\nThis is a persistent software-production fabric, not a conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Rejected candidates remain isolated, and the\\nreview reasons become residue for a second software-engineering revision stage.\\nDeclared writable paths are enforced by the tool carrier rather than trusted to a\\nprompt.\\n\\n## The solve loop ([src/solve-loop.mjs](src/solve-loop.mjs))\\n\\nMAPE-K over a working tree:\\n\\n1. **Route** — if an upfront difficulty estimate is at/above the threshold, skip free\\n   rounds and escalate straight to `claude -p` (don't waste rounds on research-hard work).\\n2. **Generate → Apply → Test** — up to `maxFreeRounds` on free inference; each failed\\n   round feeds its test output back as context (this is the Analyze→Plan feedback).\\n3. **Escalate** — if free rounds are exhausted without passing tests, escalate to\\n   `claude -p`, then re-run tests to confirm.\\n4. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, not the default — used as a quality gate and\\n  for problems above a difficulty threshold, because it is the expensive resource.\\n\\nThis is a persistent software-production fabric, not a conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, not the default — used as a quality gate and\\n  for problems above a difficulty threshold, because it is the expensive resource.\\n\\nThis is a persistent software-production fabric, not a conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. free-compute-dev\\n\\nAn autonomous software-development harness built on the firm's stated economics:\\n\\n- **Default effort = contributed compute.** Patch generation and iteration run on\\n  the cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, not the default — used as a quality gate and\\n  for problems above a difficulty threshold, because it is the expensive resource.\\n\\nThis is a persistent software-production fabric, not a conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Rejected candidates remain isolated, and the\\nreview reasons become residue for a second software-engineering revision stage.\\nDeclared writable paths are enforced by the tool carrier rather than trusted to a\\nprompt.\\n\\n## The solve loop ([src/solve-loop.mjs](src/solve-loop.mjs))\\n\\nMAPE-K over a working tree:\\n\\n1. **Route** — if an upfront difficulty estimate is at/above the threshold, skip free\\n   rounds and escalate straight to `claude -p` (don't waste rounds on research-hard work).\\n2. **Generate → Apply → Test** — up to `maxFreeRounds` on free inference; each failed\\n   round feeds its test output back as context (this is the Analyze→Plan feedback).\\n3. **Escalate** — if free rounds are exhausted without passing tests, escalate to\\n   `claude -p`, then re-run tests to confirm.\\n4. cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. conversational coding\\nwrapper. free-compute-dev\\n\\nAn autonomous software-development harness built on the firm's stated economics:\\n\\n- **Default effort = contributed compute.** Patch generation and iteration run on\\n  the cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, not the default — used as a quality gate and\\n  for problems above a difficulty threshold, because it is the expensive resource.\\n\\nThis is a persistent software-production fabric, not a conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Rejected candidates remain isolated, and the\\nreview reasons become residue for a second software-engineering revision stage.\\nDeclared writable paths are enforced by the tool carrier rather than trusted to a\\nprompt.\\n\\n## The solve loop ([src/solve-loop.mjs](src/solve-loop.mjs))\\n\\nMAPE-K over a working tree:\\n\\n1. **Route** — if an upfront difficulty estimate is at/above the threshold, skip free\\n   rounds and escalate straight to `claude -p` (don't waste rounds on research-hard work).\\n2. **Generate → Apply → Test** — up to `maxFreeRounds` on free inference; each failed\\n   round feeds its test output back as context (this is the Analyze→Plan feedback).\\n3. **Escalate** — if free rounds are exhausted without passing tests, escalate to\\n   `claude -p`, then re-run tests to confirm.\\n4. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. free-compute-dev\\n\\nAn autonomous software-development harness built on the firm's stated economics:\\n\\n- **Default effort = contributed compute.** Patch generation and iteration run on\\n  the cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, not the default — used as a quality gate and\\n  for problems above a difficulty threshold, because it is the expensive resource.\\n\\nThis is a persistent software-production fabric, not a conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. free-compute-dev\\n\\nAn autonomous software-development harness built on the firm's stated economics:\\n\\n- **Default effort = contributed compute.** Patch generation and iteration run on\\n  the cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, not the default — used as a quality gate and\\n  for problems above a difficulty threshold, because it is the expensive resource.\\n\\nThis is a persistent software-production fabric, not a conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. free-compute-dev\\n\\nAn autonomous software-development harness built on the firm's stated economics:\\n\\n- **Default effort = contributed compute.** Patch generation and iteration run on\\n  the cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, not the default — used as a quality gate and\\n  for problems above a difficulty threshold, because it is the expensive resource.\\n\\nThis is a persistent software-production fabric, not a conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Rejected candidates remain isolated, and the\\nreview reasons become residue for a second software-engineering revision stage.\\nDeclared writable paths are enforced by the tool carrier rather than trusted to a\\nprompt.\\n\\n## The solve loop ([src/solve-loop.mjs](src/solve-loop.mjs))\\n\\nMAPE-K over a working tree:\\n\\n1. **Route** — if an upfront difficulty estimate is at/above the threshold, skip free\\n   rounds and escalate straight to `claude -p` (don't waste rounds on research-hard work).\\n2. **Generate → Apply → Test** — up to `maxFreeRounds` on free inference; each failed\\n   round feeds its test output back as context (this is the Analyze→Plan feedback).\\n3. **Escalate** — if free rounds are exhausted without passing tests, escalate to\\n   `claude -p`, then re-run tests to confirm.\\n4. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. Later missions recall similar verified\\nactions. conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. free-compute-dev\\n\\nAn autonomous software-development harness built on the firm's stated economics:\\n\\n- **Default effort = contributed compute.** Patch generation and iteration run on\\n  the cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, not the default — used as a quality gate and\\n  for problems above a difficulty threshold, because it is the expensive resource.\\n\\nThis is a persistent software-production fabric, not a conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Rejected candidates remain isolated, and the\\nreview reasons become residue for a second software-engineering revision stage.\\nDeclared writable paths are enforced by the tool carrier rather than trusted to a\\nprompt.\\n\\n## The solve loop ([src/solve-loop.mjs](src/solve-loop.mjs))\\n\\nMAPE-K over a working tree:\\n\\n1. **Route** — if an upfront difficulty estimate is at/above the threshold, skip free\\n   rounds and escalate straight to `claude -p` (don't waste rounds on research-hard work).\\n2. **Generate → Apply → Test** — up to `maxFreeRounds` on free inference; each failed\\n   round feeds its test output back as context (this is the Analyze→Plan feedback).\\n3. **Escalate** — if free rounds are exhausted without passing tests, escalate to\\n   `claude -p`, then re-run tests to confirm.\\n4. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory. cheapest sufficient endpoint currently admitted by LISS (today Groq, Gemini,\\n  GitHub Models, OpenRouter when available, and later private GPU workers).\\n- **`claude -p` is the gated exception**, conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. free-compute-dev\\n\\nAn autonomous software-development harness built on the firm's stated economics:\\n\\n- **Default effort = contributed compute.** Patch generation and iteration run on\\n  the conversational coding\\nwrapper. A caller can submit an objective and leave. The fabric observes the\\nterritory, contracts parallel inference, executes bounded tools, verifies\\ncandidates, integrates one without overwriting concurrent work, and records the\\nsuccessful trajectory for reuse.\\n\\n## Live result\\n\\nOn 2026-07-19, three isolated workers contracted Groq, Gemini, and GitHub Models\\nthrough the persistent LISS broker. They made 17 useful tool decisions over eight\\nwaves. Gemini independently navigated to `src/executor.mjs`, derived a two-edit\\nrepair for a real temporary-directory leak, passed the package suite in\\nisolation, and the runtime atomically integrated and reverified it. No interactive\\nmodel call supplied the patch. The first run also taught the deterministic carrier\\nto accept providers' native JSON action dialects and structured `{search,replace}`\\nedit arrays.\\n\\nThe next unattended queued mission exposed a task-class capability boundary: three\\ncheap actors could not author a semantically valid early-quorum regression. The\\nbounded residue was resubmitted through the queue to Claude with provider-enforced\\nJSON Schema. Claude inspected the test and runtime, authored the regression, and\\nthe queue integrated it after verification. The resulting 26-test suite proves\\nearly quorum, dead-worker claim abandonment, protected-border integration, and the\\ndurable carrier itself. The failed cheap trajectory remains evidence for future\\ntask-class pricing instead of being hidden.\\n\\n## Operating surfaces\\n\\n- `run-union-dev-mission mission.json` runs one objective through parallel isolated\\n  tool workers and a verification/integration gate.\\n- `run-union-dev-program program.json` asks multiple cloud planners for acyclic\\n  mission DAGs, validates them, and executes the cheapest valid plan until the\\n  declared program acceptance command passes.\\n- `submit-union-dev-mission mission.json` and `run-union-dev-worker` provide a\\n  durable queue, claims, heartbeats, stale-claim recovery, and unattended service.\\n- `abandon-union-dev-mission exact-id reason` terminally settles work whose worker\\n  was deliberately stopped, preventing stale recovery from purchasing obsolete\\n  inference again.\\n- LISS's persistent broker accepts batches through a filesystem spool as well as a\\n  Unix socket. Sandboxed workers need neither network access nor provider keys;\\n  they atomically signal jobs through the spool while the one broker owns cloud\\n  access, pricing, concurrency, replay, and the append-only settlement journal.\\n\\nEach worker can `list_files`, `search`, `read`, apply exact edits, run the declared\\nverification/acceptance gates, and invoke only commands pre-admitted by the mission.\\nCandidate workspaces are copies; integration compares source digests and classifies\\na concurrent source change as a protected border instead of overwriting it.\\n\\nAn unresolved base phase is automatically re-contracted as `software-engineering`\\nwork requiring schema-validated actions. LISS then quotes only suppliers with that\\ncapability instead of repeatedly buying cheap syntactic completions. Successful\\nbase→escalation routes are appended by task class; a later mission of that class\\nstarts at the witnessed sufficient stage unless its manifest explicitly refuses\\nlearned routing. Program-DAG missions use the same pipeline.\\n\\nExecution-passing candidates are not integrated on that evidence alone. Unless a\\nmission explicitly declines semantic review, three independently sharded cloud\\nreviewers compare the changed source to the original objective and constraints.\\nA valid-review majority is required. Rejected candidates remain isolated, and the\\nreview reasons become residue for a second software-engineering revision stage.\\nDeclared writable paths are enforced by the tool carrier rather than trusted to a\\nprompt.\\n\\n## The solve loop ([src/solve-loop.mjs](src/solve-loop.mjs))\\n\\nMAPE-K over a working tree:\\n\\n1. **Route** — if an upfront difficulty estimate is at/above the threshold, skip free\\n   rounds and escalate straight to `claude -p` (don't waste rounds on research-hard work).\\n2. **Generate → Apply → Test** — up to `maxFreeRounds` on free inference; each failed\\n   round feeds its test output back as context (this is the Analyze→Plan feedback).\\n3. **Escalate** — if free rounds are exhausted without passing tests, escalate to\\n   `claude -p`, then re-run tests to confirm.\\n4. Return `solved-free | solved-escalated | failed` with a full round log.\\n\\nEvery dependency (`generatePatch`, `applyPatch`, `runTests`, `escalate`, `difficulty`) is\\ninjectable, so the escalation *policy* is tested deterministically with mocks\\n([test/solve-loop.test.mjs](test/solve-loop.test.mjs)) without spending real inference.\\n\\n## Recursive improvement\\n\\nEvery run appends its tool/result trajectory.
