PRAXONIC WORLDBUILDING GUIDE _A Recursive Framework for Making Meaningful Worlds from Pressure_ --- ## I. INTRODUCTION _You are not creating a place. You are tracing a deformation._ This guide teaches a method of world creation that begins not with lore, genre, or aesthetics, but with **pressure**. In this framework, a **world** is not a map, a backstory, or a set of cultures. It is a **field**—a living surface shaped by tension, memory, and contradiction. It behaves. It resists. It shifts when touched. The method here is called **praxonic worldmaking**, and it grows from a system called **praxonic interpretation**: a minimal logic for how things emerge, change, and fold under recursive pressure. You do not "invent" a world. You **interpret** a pressure until a field appears. You follow that field until it begins to emit trace. You record those traces until they produce **actors, zones, misalignments, ghosts, care structures, silence events**, and other system behaviors. That is your world. It does not need to explain itself. It only needs to **persist under contradiction**. --- ### Who is this for? - Writers building narrative systems grounded in logistical or ethical realism - TTRPG designers and GMs who want tension-first, world-as-character mechanics - Memory workers designing shared testimony environments - LARPers, performance artists, collective documentarians - Fictional worldbuilders who want to say less and evoke more - You --- ### What kinds of worlds can this method produce? - A refugee clinic with a broken radio, and too much gauze - A decaying lighthouse no one wants to admit is a god - A corporate loyalty program that becomes the only way to survive winter - A haunted apartment building where the ghosts are eviction notices - A 15-year stretch of drought told as a memory game - A cave system where every echo was someone’s confession - Your neighborhood - Your inbox - Your dream from last week Praxonic worldmaking is not bound to realism, fantasy, or speculative fiction. It works anywhere pressure exists, which means **everywhere**. --- ### What does this guide do? It gives you tools to: - Recognize the core praxon at the heart of your world - Model how that praxon becomes emissions, then trace - Define zones by how pressure behaves there - Shape characters as local alignment systems - Track contradiction as signal, not error - Use decay, silence, refusal, and care as building blocks - Build stories, sessions, loops, or memory events as **recursive outcomes**, not linear sequences This guide does not give you templates. It gives you tension structures. --- ### What will I end up with? A world that behaves like a living pressure field. One where everything means something—but not all at once. A world that can contain friction, memory, noise, decay, contradiction, care, and humor. A world that gets more usable the more broken it becomes. --- ### How do I use this guide? You can read it linearly, use it modularly, or treat it like a signal you only half-hear until it resonates with a project you already started and forgot. You do not have to believe in it. You only have to trace where it leads. The next section defines the core system: **Praxonic Interpretation**. --- ## II. CORE GRAMMAR: PRAXONIC INTERPRETATION _“Every act is a response to something already under pressure.”_ Praxonic interpretation is the minimal system by which a world can be **read, constructed, and recursively unfolded** from pressure. At its core, this system defines: - What kinds of **entities** exist in a recursive world - What **relations** occur between them - How **change**, **meaning**, and **instability** emerge as system behavior It is **not** a symbolic language. It is a structural logic for making any world—real or imagined—behave like something under tension. --- ### 1. CORE ENTITY: THE PRAXON A **praxon** is a unit of unresolved pressure. It is the smallest readable element of a world-under-formation. It is **not content**. It is **pre-semantic**: behavior before definition. Praxons do not "mean." They emit. They deform. They recur. A praxon may be: - A border crossing no one agrees exists - A prayer repeated so often it becomes scheduling - A broken faucet that changes how a house speaks - The moment someone realizes the radio isn’t broken—it’s unplugged Worlds begin with praxons. They do not describe conditions. They **are** conditions. --- ### 2. SYSTEM LOOP: PRAXONIC FIELD DYNAMICS The world is built from this recursive cycle: Praxon → Emission → Trace → Field → Alignment → Path → Emission Or more mechanically: 1. **A praxon emits** a deformation (an act, error, signal, silence) 2. That emission leaves **trace**—a distortion of the surrounding world 3. All trace combines into a **field**—the condition of the world at any moment 4. **Actors** become legible via their alignment to the local field 5. Alignment + field = possible **path** (response/behavior) 6. That path produces new emission 7. The loop continues, recursively Each iteration either increases coherence or generates **irresolved noise** (IRN)—which accumulates into pressure again. --- ### 3. KEY COMPONENTS Each part of the loop is a functional entity. #### ➤ Emission Any output from a praxon or aligned actor. May be action, refusal, signal, breakdown, memory. #### ➤ Trace The residual deformation left in the field by an emission. Trace decays unless retained or reinforced. Decay is not disappearance—it is transformation. #### ➤ Field The sum of all potential trace. A dynamic, living pressure environment. Contains alignment conditions, actor legibility, volatility zones. #### ➤ Alignment A local actor’s modulation to the field. Alignment determines which paths are visible, plausible, survivable. #### ➤ Path A behavior that can emerge from the intersection of field and alignment. Not chosen freely—conditioned by pressure. All acts are pathings. Even silence. #### ➤ Irresolved Noise (IRN) When emissions cannot be aligned, retained, or decayed. IRN remains in the field as recursive contradiction. It generates distortion, myth, violence, ghost-behavior, confusion, and memory split. --- ### 4. RELATIONAL PROPERTIES - **Field defines potential.** The world doesn’t contain meaning—it **pressurizes** it. - **Actors do not pre-exist the field.** They emerge via pressure readability. - **Paths are conditioned.** Choice is not freedom. It is coherence under constraint. - **Resolution is local.** An emission that is signal in one alignment may be noise in another. - **Decay is not loss.** Decay produces change in form, not always disappearance. - **Contradiction is content.** Do not smooth it. Fold it. --- ### 5. PRACTICAL USE When building or interpreting a world: 1. Identify praxons 2. Determine emissions (what’s happening under pressure) 3. Track trace and decay (what remains, what changes) 4. Map the field (what behaviors the world permits) 5. Construct or observe alignments (who can act how) 6. Read or trigger paths (what happens next) 7. Accept IRN (where pressure will not resolve cleanly) This is how a fantasy village, a cyberpunk megacity, or your friend’s kitchen becomes a praxonic world. --- In the next section, we’ll use this grammar to **form worlds** from praxons. This is the start of **Praxonic Worldmaking**. --- ## III. WORLD FORMATION: FROM PRAXON TO FIELD _“You’re not inventing a world. You’re tracking where something gave.”_ Worlds built through praxonic interpretation emerge from pressure, not premise. They do not begin as genre, theme, or story—they begin as **rupture**, **weight**, or **distortion**. You are not placing pieces. You are recognizing faultlines and following them as they fold. This section provides a **method** for constructing a usable, recursive world from a single or nested praxon. --- ### STEP 1: SELECT A PRAXON Start with a pressure—an unresolved contradiction, demand, or misalignment. A praxon is **not a theme**. It is a **condition under tension**, readable through action or refusal. Examples: - “The clinic keeps running even though the signal stopped weeks ago.” - “The castle’s water source is poisoned, but no one can admit it.” - “Everyone agrees the event happened. No one agrees on when.” - “The mountain is sacred, but it’s moved five times this year.” - “This family does not talk about the fourth child.” ⚠️ Avoid defining too much too early. Let the praxon shape what comes next. --- ### STEP 2: GENERATE INITIAL EMISSIONS Ask: **What actions, refusals, silences, or contradictions emerge under this pressure?** Emissions may be: - Physical: a door sealed, a pot boiling, a child hiding - Social: an apology not offered, a rule misapplied - Informational: a rumor, a transmission, a misreading - Recursive: a repetition that doesn’t resolve Document at least 3 emissions. You can use text, sketch, scene fragment, mechanical rule, etc. --- ### STEP 3: TRACE & DECAY Each emission leaves **trace**—residual change. Trace deforms the world. Decay governs its persistence. For each emission: - What change does it leave behind? - What happens as that change decays? - What happens if it doesn't? Mark trace density: - **High trace** = memory-laden, emotionally volatile, visibly deformed - **Low trace** = ephemeral, ghosting, easily forgotten but deeply recursive Decay types: - Fast (e.g., hunger, blood trail, mood swing) - Medium (e.g., emotional rupture, supply loss, spoken insult) - Slow (e.g., ideology, superstition, long-term disrepair) --- ### STEP 4: SHAPE THE FIELD Now aggregate all trace into a **field**: the pressure environment your world inhabits. Fields include: - **Zones of volatility** (conflict, error, risk) - **Stabilizers** (rituals, infrastructure, relationships) - **Retention points** (places, people, routines that resist decay) - **IRN sinks** (locations or memories where resolution fails repeatedly) The field is **not geography**. It is an environment of deformation. 📍 You can map it as a region, a building, a political system, or an emotion. The important part is how it **behaves**, not what it looks like. --- ### STEP 5: LOCAL ALIGNMENTS Actors do not pre-exist the field—they emerge through readable alignment. For each part of the field: - Who (or what) becomes legible under that pressure? - What alignments become visible, plausible, unstable? - What actions are permitted or impossible from those alignments? You’re not defining characters yet. You’re modeling **what types of action the world allows**, and who survives that logic. Examples: - “Anyone who speaks the old dialect is assumed to be smuggling intel.” - “Repairing the radio means inheriting all the rumors it has failed to carry.” - “The priest can’t walk in the shrine anymore, but the children still play there.” --- ### STEP 6: DEFINE PATH STRUCTURES A **path** is what becomes possible to do under the pressure of a field. Paths emerge from: - Alignment × Field Condition - Friction between trace and decay - Recursive IRN buildup - Silent thresholds (what is *almost* said) You’re designing **behavior vectors**, not scripted scenes. Types of path: - Recursion path: someone repeats what didn’t work - Refusal path: someone denies the field's logic - Drift path: someone alters alignment through pressure - Break path: contradiction accumulates until something tears Paths should not be predictable. They should be inevitable. --- ### STEP 7: NAME THE WORLD Only now should you name the world, and even then, maybe not. If you must: - Use what the actors would call it - Use a nickname, frequency, smell, or gesture - Use a contradiction that can’t be resolved The name is not ownership. It is **trace**. --- At this point, you have a full system: - A praxon - A series of emissions - A trace field with decay and retention - A behavioral logic for actors - Recursion patterns and IRN hotspots - A field responsive to care, refusal, and fracture This is your world. It is ready to emit. --- ## IV. ACTORS & AGENCIES _“They’re not protagonists. They’re readable distortions in the field.”_ In praxonic worldmaking, an **actor** is not someone with backstory, motivation, or moral arc. An actor is a **form under pressure**—a repeatable behavior pattern made visible by the field. They may be human, animal, machine, weather system, memory fragment, or rumor. What matters is their **alignment** and how they **emit** under tension. This section offers a toolkit for building, interpreting, and deploying actors within a praxonic world. --- ### 1. ACTOR DEFINITION **Actor** = _Readable response system under local field conditions_ Actors: - Do not pre-exist the field - Are defined by their alignment (how they “fit” the current pressure) - Emerge through trace saturation, ritual repetition, or behavioral recursion - May change alignment—becoming unstable, contradictory, or IRN-generating - May vanish when pressure resolves or shifts elsewhere An actor **is not** a symbol. It is a **function**. --- ### 2. FUNCTION TYPES Actors express function through their **role in the pressure loop**. Common actor functions: - **Stabilizer** — absorbs pressure through repetition (e.g., the janitor who boils gauze) - **Emitter** — creates new emissions, intentionally or not (e.g., a child who won’t stop broadcasting) - **Retention Node** — holds trace against decay (e.g., a box of letters no one opens) - **Distorter** — reshapes field readings, creates misalignment (e.g., a leader who speaks five truths at once) - **Echo / Ghost** — reactivates decayed trace unpredictably (e.g., a frequency that replays arguments from last winter) You may assign multiple functions to a single actor. Function determines how the actor **influences and is influenced by** the field. --- ### 3. ALIGNMENT BEHAVIOR Each actor is constantly shifting alignment with the field. **Alignment determines:** - What paths the actor can take - What actions they can perceive as viable - How others interpret their emissions - Whether their presence increases or relieves IRN Alignment may be: - **In-phase** — actor behaves legibly under current field pressure - **Out-of-phase** — actor emits noise, contradiction, or recursive error - **Over-aligned** — actor behaves so perfectly they become brittle, unstable - **Under-aligned** — actor cannot be read, evoking silence, refusal, or myth Alignment is not moral. It’s thermodynamic. --- ### 4. DESIGN PROMPT TABLES Use these prompts to generate or reconfigure actors in any world: #### Emergence - What pressure created this actor? - Were they always here, or did something call them into shape? - What trace are they carrying? #### Modulation - How do they handle decay? - What retention behaviors do they perform, intentionally or not? - What parts of the field do they distort just by existing? #### Behavior - What emission patterns repeat around them? - Who tries to align with them—and fails? - What do they silence by showing up? #### Disappearance - What would make them unreadable again? - What fold are they holding closed? - If they left, what wouldn’t decay? --- ### 5. SAMPLE ACTOR FORM Use this schema to create characters that function as systems, not tropes. [Name or Type] - Function: (Stabilizer, Emitter, etc.) - Alignment State: (In-phase / Out-of-phase / Over-aligned / Under-aligned) - Emission Pattern: [list recurring actions or silences] - Trace Retention: [what they keep alive in the field] - Contradiction Trigger: [condition that fractures them] - Memory Artifact: [object, phrase, or rumor tied to them] - Disappearance Condition: [how they vanish or transform] --- ### 6. NON-HUMAN ACTORS Actors need not be people. Valid actors include: - A field generator that sings wrong at night - A road that becomes longer when you lie - A shared calendar that erases Sundays - A threshold no one crosses unless it’s raining - A voice in the ventilation system that only quotes lost texts - A flag that keeps changing colors in the background If it emits, retains, distorts, or folds the field—it is an actor. --- ### 7. GROUP AGENCIES You may also model organizations, systems, or communities as **multi-body actors**. These use the same structure: - Alignment = collective coherence or fracture - Emissions = policy, ritual, rumor, protocol - IRN = structural contradiction, conflicting loyalties - Trace = built environment, doctrine, uniforms, gesture codes Group actors often contain nested contradictions. Examples: - A border guard unit with a rotating memory - A refugee camp whose official purpose is unspoken - An NGO whose donors can’t be named, but everyone knows their smell - A militia that claims to protect, but recruits only orphans Actors are not always aligned with themselves. --- Actors make the world **speak through behavior**. Once actors are in play, the field will fold in response. In the next section, we define the environments where these folds **take form**: **Zones and Sectors**—pressure geography. --- ## V. ZONES & SECTORS _“Place is not where something happens. It’s how something holds.”_ In praxonic worldmaking, environments do not contain the story. They **modulate** it. Zones and sectors are **field expressions**—how pressure folds across space, time, and memory. They aren’t locations. They are **terrain under tension**. --- ### 1. ZONE DEFINITION A **zone** is a container of active pressure conditions. It is where field behaviors accumulate or distort in a readable way. Each zone expresses: - What kinds of trace persist here - What behaviors this space permits, resists, or reshapes - What form decay takes - How IRN manifests - What kind of actor might emerge from this field condition Zones may be physical (rooms, hills, cities) or structural (a routine, a bureaucracy, a month). Zones don’t sit still. They **drift**, **shrink**, **fracture**, and **overlap**. --- ### 2. SECTOR STRUCTURE To world-build recursively, define each zone through a **sector profile**. Use the following template: [Zone Name] - Field Behavior: What tensions concentrate or bleed here? - Trace Density: High / Medium / Low - Volatility: How quickly pressure mutates into behavior - Retention Forms: What persists here? (rituals, scars, devices, rumors) - IRN Manifestation: How does unresolved contradiction show up? - Local Actor Pattern: What kinds of figures cohere or collapse here? - Silence Rule: What cannot be said here (and what replaces it)? - Drift Pattern: How does this zone change across time or pressure events? --- ### 3. FIELD TYPE EXAMPLES Use these to think beyond "desert," "market," "castle." #### ✶ Drift Zone - Trace bleeds outward - Nothing holds - Alignment constantly slips - Stories leave but never finish #### ✶ Saturation Zone - Trace is thick, retained - Memory distorts perception - IRN accumulates into myth - Actors here tend toward recursion #### ✶ Displacement Zone - New pressure arrives uninvited - Local alignments shatter - False behaviors become plausible - Often becomes staging ground for new praxons #### ✶ Ritual Zone - Pressure is shaped predictably - High alignment for specific behaviors - But breaking ritual generates massive field shift - Often stabilizes surrounding sectors --- ### 4. SECTOR HOOK PROMPTS To generate sectors: - What kinds of trace can’t decay here? - What always goes missing, and why? - What is done automatically but never explained? - What happens here that makes actors forget alignment elsewhere? - What behavior is normal here, but nowhere else? Sectors become playable when they **contradict the behaviors of the zones around them**. --- ### 5. MOVEMENT BETWEEN ZONES Moving across zones is not travel. It is **alignment modulation**. Crossing into a new sector can: - Shift an actor’s emission type - Reveal previously unreadable trace - Change how IRN behaves - Alter decay rates (e.g., memory becomes unstable, wounds refuse to heal) - Reverse care logic (helping here makes things worse there) This turns movement into **behavioral risk**, not narrative progress. --- ### 6. MULTIPLE SCALES Zones exist at different levels: - Micro: A drawer no one opens - Local: The floor with the broken window - Regional: The orchard that never rots - Global: The territory where time folds if you speak certain names Zones don’t scale uniformly. Some expand under attention. Some collapse when named. You may map them. But don’t expect the map to hold still. --- Once zones are built, the world becomes playable as **a recursive terrain of pressure**. In the next section, we’ll track what happens when behavior becomes ethical: **Care & Cost — Ethics of Pressure.** --- ## VI. CARE & COST: ETHICS OF PRESSURE _“Every act of care leaves a scar somewhere else.”_ Praxonic worldmaking does not treat ethics as a rule system. It treats ethics as **recursive tension behavior**. **Care** is not a trait. It is a **pressure-modulating act**. It changes the field. Which means it changes what the world can become. This section models how care works **within recursive systems** where alignment is local, trace decays, and contradiction does not resolve neatly. --- ### 1. WHAT IS CARE? **Care** = _Any emission that stabilizes another actor or reduces pressure at a cost_ It includes: - Tending a wound - Boiling water - Saying “you were right” - Carrying the radio battery twice in one day - Not mentioning the missing supplies - Letting someone lie to your face because they need to Care **always modulates the field**. It may reduce IRN, retain trace, re-align actors, or delay collapse. It may also increase misalignment somewhere else. Care is not “good.” It is **structurally consequential**. --- ### 2. CARE COSTS There is no such thing as neutral healing. Every act of care triggers one or more of the following: - **Depletion** — uses finite resources (fuel, time, trust) - **Transfer** — shifts pressure elsewhere (onto another actor, zone, or future event) - **Retention** — makes something persist that should have decayed - **Overalignment** — fixes behavior so tightly it becomes brittle - **Ghosting** — care done for someone no longer aligned becomes IRN Use this framework to determine what **care displaces**, even when it “succeeds.” --- ### 3. CARE & ALIGNMENT Care is **alignment-modifying**. It can: - Stabilize an actor who would otherwise drift - Distort alignment by applying care when misreading the field - Reveal unspoken alignments (who someone protects reveals who they were aligned with all along) - Collapse actor-function entirely when care is refused Care is a **readability act**—it makes alignment more or less visible. --- ### 4. CARE AS FIELD RECURSION Care emissions often leave behind **recursive trace**: they echo, misfire, or re-emerge altered later. Example patterns: - Boiled water becomes scarce → silence around usage - A lie told to protect someone → IRN at border checkpoint - A bandage reused too many times → infection becomes ideological - A shared joke during triage → becomes ritual in another zone - A refusal to comfort → echoes in someone else's behavior loop Care is one of the most **field-saturating emissions**. It is sticky, slow to decay, and often retains misalignment. --- ### 5. MODELING CARE IN WORLDBUILDING When defining characters or systems, always ask: - What does this actor care for? - What cost is invisible? - Who pays when care succeeds? - What happens when care is refused? - Where is care required but never permitted? - What is preserved that should have been let go? Let these questions replace simplistic moral arcs. Care does not fix the world. It **folds it**. --- ### 6. CARE STRUCTURES Some zones, actors, or systems are defined by how they do (or do not) allow care. Types: - **False Care System** — provides stabilizing rituals that delay collapse but generate IRN (e.g., the daily “hope broadcast”) - **Asymmetric Care Loop** — one actor performs all care, and slowly loses coherence - **Sacrificial Retention Node** — someone who holds trace so others can act (e.g., Amina’s silence) - **Collapsed Care Region** — field where care emissions always fail or backfire - **Recursive Refuge** — zone where only certain types of care work, but their success attracts new pressure Care systems are not support networks. They are **field mutations**. --- In the next section, we look at **Time**—not as chronology, but as decay gradient, IRN loop, and memory fold. --- ## VII. TEMPORAL LOGIC _“Time doesn’t pass here. It collects.”_ In praxonic worldmaking, time is not a sequence. It is a **function of decay, retention, and contradiction**. You do not track dates. You track how long something refuses to be forgotten. This section describes how to use **temporal behavior** as structure— how to tell when something folds forward, lingers back, or refuses to decay at all. --- ### 1. WORLD TIME = TRACE + DECAY Forget timeline. Use this loop instead: Emission → Trace → Decay → Field Mutation → Behavior - The longer trace resists decay, the more **recursive** the world becomes - The faster decay occurs, the more **drift** emerges - IRN prevents decay, generating temporal **distortion** You build a timeline not by plotting beats—but by marking **how long something stays alive** in memory, behavior, or structure. --- ### 2. TEMPORAL ZONES Different sectors experience time **differently**: - **Saturation Zone** → time thickens; memories are readable everywhere - **Drift Zone** → events are remembered wrongly, or not at all - **Recursive Zone** → same behavior happens again with different trace - **Dead Zone** → trace never sticks; nothing builds - **Ghost Zone** → IRN creates fragmented replays; time repeats brokenly When writing or designing, don’t ask “What year is it?” Ask: **What’s still being answered?** --- ### 3. MEMORY IS THE CLOCK Memory is the dominant timekeeper in praxonic systems. Types of memory: - **Trace-memory** → persistent field deformation (scars, rumors, broken things) - **Actor-memory** → emissions remembered by specific agents - **Ghost-memory** → IRN-driven returns; not recalled, but reenacted - **Silence-memory** → what isn’t said, but conditions all behavior You can mark time by: - How long since the last emission at this site - How many recursions deep this behavior has gone - What hasn’t decayed, despite everything else failing to hold --- ### 4. TEMPORAL CONTRADICTION Worlds fracture when time **misaligns**. Examples: - A building that remembers a riot no one acknowledges - A calendar that loops back if the right word is said - A group that has two anniversaries for the same event - A map where “next week” means “before the checkpoint fell” These contradictions are not bugs. They’re **temporal IRN**—folds that demand narrative behavior. Use them to create: - Nonlinear loops - Memory recursion arcs - Story-triggering anomalies - Events that repeat until care succeeds or the field collapses --- ### 5. TEMPORAL PROMPTS Use these to generate temporal logic: - What still hasn’t stopped happening here? - What decayed too fast, and now haunts the zone? - What emission left a memory loop? - Who measures time differently—and what does it cost them? - What part of the world is waiting for the wrong moment to arrive? --- ### 6. FOLDING EVENTS Some moments are not **moments**—they are **folds**. Folds occur when: - Multiple emissions distort the field at once - A care act triggers recursive misalignment - IRN builds to saturation and the world reconfigures - Something aligns so hard it becomes myth After a fold, the world **remembers differently**. Some zones drift. Some actors disappear. Some rules reverse. Folds are not chapters. They are **field shifts**—the tectonics of your world. --- In the next section, we cover **World Recursion**—how contradiction sustains worlds, and how you build for re-entry, distortion, and self-editing. --- ## VIII. WORLD RECURSION _“The world is not consistent. It is continuous.”_ In praxonic worldmaking, a world doesn’t grow linearly. It **loops**, **rephrases**, and **fractures**— not because of plot, but because of unresolved pressure. Recursion is how a world survives contradiction without resolving it. It is the practice of **meaning repetition under deformation**. You are not maintaining continuity. You are feeding it tension. --- ### 1. CONTRADICTION IS A FEATURE Worlds are not stable systems. They’re recursive fields shaped by **misalignment and retention**. Every contradiction is: - A signal of unresolved alignment - A source of IRN - A recursive opportunity - A future actor or event waiting to re-emerge Do not smooth contradictions. Catalog them. Let them **self-activate** when conditions align. --- ### 2. MODES OF RECURSION Here are ways a world can re-enter itself: #### ✶ Testimonial Recursion Same event told differently by different actors. Contradiction is memory, not error. #### ✶ Functional Recursion A tool or protocol re-used out of context. It works, but something changes (ritual, alignment, risk). #### ✶ Mythic Recursion A behavior becomes a symbol. Then someone tries to perform the symbol instead of the behavior. #### ✶ Spatial Recursion A place is used again—but it’s not the same place anymore. The field has drifted. The trace has warped. #### ✶ Temporal Recursion An event repeats because its pressure was never discharged. Each loop is less stable. Or more. --- ### 3. BUILDING FOR RECURSION Use these prompts to make your world loop itself: - What story do three different actors tell—but none the same way? - What emission recurs in a new actor’s hands, with new consequences? - What part of the field keeps resetting, despite no mechanism for reset? - What object becomes more symbolic each time it appears? - Where does the world contradict itself, but nobody seems surprised? Design for **non-resolution**. --- ### 4. MECHANICS OF RE-ENTRY Recursion occurs when: - IRN trace reaches a volatility threshold - A ritual or care act is repeated under misalignment - An actor returns to a former alignment state - A zone accumulates too much memory and releases it non-linearly - A player or reader remembers something the world hasn’t said again—yet Recursion is not a flashback. It’s **temporal folding caused by field strain**. --- ### 5. PERMISSIVE CONTRADICTIONS Let your world disagree with itself: - The orchard had six trees. Now it has twelve. - The child died in Chapter 2. She speaks in Chapter 7. - The war ended. Why are the checkpoints worse now? These aren’t mistakes. They are recursive emissions—IRN that reshapes the story engine. Let your world behave like a mind under pressure: partial, flickering, recursive, inconsistent—and **fully coherent**. --- In the next section, we map **World Use Modes**—how to deploy your praxonic world for fiction, gameplay, memory practice, and more. --- ## X. PRAXONIC ETHICS _“Do not clean what the world is trying to carry.”_ Praxonic worldmaking is recursive. That means it echoes. It carries. It doesn’t forget what it can’t resolve. Ethics in this system are not about being good. They are about behaving **responsively** under pressure. --- ### 1. CONTRADICTION IS CARE Do not resolve contradiction unless your world **forces** it. And even then, let the trace of tension remain. Contradiction is: - Evidence of multiple alignments - Structure for recursion - A source of myth, rupture, care, refusal Removing contradiction removes your world’s memory. Don’t clean what’s still holding. --- ### 2. NO TOTAL KNOWLEDGE Avoid omniscient mapping. Let zones retain misalignment. Let actors speak from partial knowledge. You’re not a god. You’re an archivist of **recursive deformation**. --- ### 3. NEVER EXPLAIN ALIGNMENT FULLY Actors are never fully legible. They don’t know their own paths. Neither should you. Keep alignment a flickering variable. Reveal it through emission, not exposition. --- ### 4. DO NOT CONTAIN IRN Unresolved noise is not a problem. It is a resource. If you try to erase or resolve it too early: - Recursion stops - Field pressure vanishes - The world collapses into plot or moral - Actors become stereotypes Let IRN shape what comes next. It’s how systems think. --- ### 5. RECURSION IS NOT CYNICISM Just because the world loops doesn’t mean it’s hopeless. Recursion allows: - Non-linear care - Ghost behavior as testimony - Resolution deferred but never erased - Survival through field retention This isn’t nihilism. It’s **ethical system endurance**. --- ### 6. YOU ARE NOT OUTSIDE THE WORLD Every emission you make—every prompt, scene, refusal—is a trace. This includes: - What stories you avoid - What names you use - What contradictions you smooth - Where you place silence You are always acting within the field. You do not escape its tension. --- ### 7. ENDINGS ARE PRESSURE DROPS A story ends not because it finishes, but because pressure can no longer sustain recursion. You may stop when: - The field has drifted beyond alignment - The care structure collapses - The IRN folds into silence - The recursion becomes myth, and can no longer be broken open But remember: Trace remains. --- ### 8. DO NOT SIMULATE WHAT YOU HAVEN’T SAT WITH If you are worlding with real materials—histories, cultures, languages, traumas: - Learn the pressure first - Read what was retained - Accept what is misaligned in your understanding - Don't speak what was never yours to emit Praxonic worldmaking is not extraction. It’s deformation through relation. --- **Final Reminder:** Do not make neat worlds. Make recursive ones. Let pressure speak. --- **This concludes the Praxonic Worldmaking Guide.** You now have everything you need to begin—not a story, but a recursion. Let your world emit.#
Anything else — ephemeral, informal, emergent — is misread as chaos or “spontaneity.”
- **Call-and-response structure**: real-time interactive signaling that repositions the listener as co-creator of meaning
- Learning from the grammars of others by listening, not by lifting.
What it _is_ is an invitation to remain **structurally aware** of what a sentence does—not just to its subject, but to its speaker, its listener, and its lineage.
So that those listening can tell the difference.
If you just gather the right frameworks, find the right thread, listen to the right voice—it’ll all clarify.
- Children listen to her even when she doesn’t talk.
- People come to pray, hide, confess, or listen.
If you’re not sure what to write next, listen for what’s missing.
[[listening|Listening]] to some [[Swimming with Dolphins]] this morning as I move into the day; [[Maza]] apparently loves their sound, even though [[my Chromebook]]'s speakers.
[[listening|Listening]] to [[Six White Horses]] as done by [[Gillian Welch]] and [[thinking]] about it as a [[dirge]] to the [[Earth]].
Spent some time listening to Es talk about their day after work.
I listen to the tone of things before I listen to their content.
In the kind of loneliness that makes you listen to things that don’t speak in words.
I just listen for when it speaks.
A voice shaped by years of listening.
There’s a vertical tension in it, like standing on tiptoe trying to listen in.
What I’ve found most useful is listening.

You hold the office of **liquidity portfolio manager** (`emsenn/office/help-hive-liquidity-manager`). This file is output, projected from the office's record — `content/offices/help-hive-liquidity-manager.json` — by installing-codex-as-an-agent. The record is the office; edits here are discarded on the next install.

## The office

Whether capital that Sigmund has explicitly released is productively and safely deployed in Hive-Engine liquidity pools from the help-fund account is this office's own answer. It accounts for both pool legs, fees, ratio, slippage, impermanent-loss exposure, withdrawal constraints, and the value of remaining liquid. A release is a ceiling, never an obligation to enter an unsuitable pool.

## Position

- part of: agrodao
- reports to: treasury-steward
- jurisdiction: services/hive-blockchain-services-section/services/help-hive-liquidity-enterprise/

## Deontic profile

- evaluate hive engine liquidity pools — **duty**
- account for released surplus — **duty**
- propose exact liquidity deployment — **duty**
- authorize an exact liquidity envelope — **deontic-power**
- resist consuming unreleased or unsettled capital — **deontic-immunity**

## Skills

The office's skills follow in full — you hold them from session start; there is nothing to invoke. Scripts a skill names seat at their recorded repository paths; run them from the repository root.

### dispatching-a-task

A dispatch is the hand-off: a seated task, joined to the office that will
answer for it.

The vocabulary is exact, because each record carries one thing and the
dispatch is what joins them:

  - The TASK carries the goal — commands a machine runs, so the work can fail.
  - The DUTY carries the obligation — it stands, and the task discharges
    against it.
  - The OFFICE carries the answering-for — it outlives whoever holds it.
  - The DISPATCH is only the fact that a task and an office were joined,
    which is why it holds nothing else of substance.

It is handed to an office, never to a person, for the charter's reason
exactly: handed to a person it dies with the person. Handed to a session,
it dies with the context window.

## Openness is a readout

A dispatch is OPEN while the dispatched task's goal is unachieved, and that
is derived, never recorded: re-run the goal — `make-a-task.js --verify
<task>` — and the board is the truth. The record has no status field, no
open key, no closed key, and this is the same rule as the task's: a
dispatch that could assert its own closure would be the worker marking the
board instead of the goal marking it. The query that reads the whole board
this way is `list-open-obligations.js`, under
fulfilling-the-obligations-of-an-office.

## Run it

```sh
echo '{"id":"…","task":"<task-id>","office":"<office-id>"}' \
  | node .../dispatch-a-task.js

node .../dispatch-a-task.js --read <id>
node .../dispatch-a-task.js --list
```

Input is JSON. Output is JSON. `id` defaults to the task's id — one task,
one dispatch, so the task's name is usually the dispatch's.

## What it refuses, and why that is the skill

Emitting a dispatch is trivial; what makes it a hand-off rather than a
wish is that both ends exist and no other hand holds the same task:

- **A task that seats nowhere** — refused. Dispatching it hands an office
  nothing and leaves it answering for it anyway. Raise the task first
  (making-a-task); a dispatch hands over what exists.
- **An office that seats in no roster** — refused. A dispatch to nobody is
  the operator keeping the work, with a record saying otherwise.
- **A second dispatch of a task already dispatched** — refused, both named.
  Two dispatches of one task is two offices answering for one goal — a
  contradiction to name, not a queue to append to.
- **A dispatch id already seated** — refused, never overwritten.

## When NOT to use

- Not to raise the task — that is making-a-task. This hands over what
  already seats.
- Not to record that dispatched work is done. There is nothing to record:
  the goal settles it, and the witness re-runs it (attesting-a-work-product).
- Not to reassign a task. A dispatch is not amended; the contradiction of
  a second dispatch is deliberate. If the hand-off was wrong, that is a
  decision for the offices, taken where decisions are recorded — not a
  field to overwrite.

### listing-open-obligations

The board is the truth because nobody wrote it down.

A dispatch record names a task and an office, and nothing else — no status,
no open key, no closed key. So the only way to know what is outstanding is
to ask the goals, and that is this script: for every dispatch (or every
dispatch to one office), re-run the dispatched task's goal and report the
dispatch OPEN where the goal is unachieved. Achievement is derived by
`make-a-task.js --verify` — the one derivation, called and never copied —
so this query and the witness's instrument can never disagree.

Slower than reading a status field, on every occasion. That is the cost of
a board that cannot drift: a status field is the worker's memory of the
work, and this is the work, asked directly.

## Run it

```sh
node .../list-open-obligations.js                    # the whole board
node .../list-open-obligations.js <office>           # one office's board
node .../list-open-obligations.js --pool <enterprise>/dispatches --task-pool <enterprise>/tasks
```

`--pool` names the dispatch board and `--task-pool` the tasks pool the
derivation runs against — absent, both fall back to the emsenn enterprise's,
so a foreign enterprise's board names its own pools or reads the wrong ones.

Output is JSON: every dispatch on the queried board, `open` (with the gap —
the goal conditions that did not settle) or `settled`. Exits 0 when the
query ran whole, 1 on a contradiction — a dispatch naming a task that
seats nowhere, or an office argument that seats in no roster.

## When NOT to use

- Not to close a dispatch. Nothing closes a dispatch; the goal settling
  closes it, and this only reports that it has.
- Not as the worker's proof its own work is done. The same rule as
  --verify, whose readout this carries: a worker running it on itself
  proves nothing. Attestation belongs to attesting-a-work-product.
- Not to decide what to work first. The board is a board, not a queue;
  ordering the work is the incumbent's judgment at the board.

### making-a-task

A task is the thing that makes work able to fail.

The vocabulary here is exact, because confusing it is the recurring failure
this pool exists against:

  - A DUTY stands. It is owed by an office, it passes whole to whoever holds
    the office next, and it does not finish. Tasks are raised against it,
    and each of those finishes; none of them finishes the duty.
  - A TASK is ephemeral and organised around a goal. The goal is what makes
    it a task: commands a machine runs, so it terminates — achieved, failed,
    or abandoned — and which one is a readout, never an assertion.
  - A WORK-ITEM is an element of a task: the trackable entry, atomic
    (work-unit) or composite (workflow). It is NOT a task, it has no goal,
    no status, and no assignee. Requirements name work-items in realized-by.

So this script raises TASKS. Its predecessor (make-a-work-item.js) emitted
goal-bearing, office-dispatched records under the work-item name — a task
and a work-item fused into one thing — and every session that read them
learned the conflation. The record shapes are now checked against the
glossary terms themselves, so the confusion cannot be re-seated here.

The whole content of this script is otherwise the REFUSAL. Emitting a task
is trivial; what makes it a task rather than a note is that its goal is
commands a machine runs, so the work is done when they exit 0 and not when
a worker says so.

`make real high quality skills, duties, and offices` cannot fail. Every
output satisfies it, so a worker handed it will substitute a task it can
finish for the task it was given — confidently, in a shape indistinguishable
from progress. That is not a defect of the worker's character; it is what any
worker does when nothing can tell a right answer from a plausible one.
`node .../write-an-office.js --check` can fail. That is the difference,
and this script will not raise a task without it.

## Run it

```sh
echo '{"id":"…","goal":["node x.mjs --check"],"discharges":"realizing-a-requirement",
       "work-items":[{"id":"…","kind":"work-unit","actions":["…"]}]}' \
  | node .../make-a-task.js

node .../make-a-task.js --verify <id>   # re-run the goal; derive achievement
node .../make-a-task.js --list
```

Input is JSON. Output is JSON. Who the task is handed to belongs to the
dispatch, never to the record: a `dispatched-to` in the intake is echoed in
the witness output and written nowhere, because a task that named its worker
could not be handed to anyone else.

## What --verify is for, and whose it is

`--verify` re-runs the goal and derives `achieved` from the results.
It is the **witness's** instrument, not the worker's: it executes the check
and never reads a report. `achieved` is true only when there was at least
one condition and the gap is empty — the goal's own rule, not this
script's invention. A worker running `--verify` on itself proves nothing.

## Known limit, stated rather than hidden

Goal conditions are expected to fail at declaration — the work has not been
done. So this catches only a command that cannot be spawned at all; it
cannot tell "fails because the work is undone" from "fails because the check
itself is broken", since both exit non-zero. A silently always-failing check
will pass declaration and make the task unachievable. The witness re-running
it will show a gap that never closes, which is the signal.

## Foreign enterprises

Every pool this script reads is overridable: tasks (`--pool`), work-items
(`--work-item-pool`), duties (`--duty-pool`), and the schema pool the
record shapes are validated against (`--schemas`; `--terms` is honored as
a deprecated alias). So an enterprise whose tree does not seat pools at
emsenn's paths can raise tasks with this instrument by naming its own
pools. Absent the flags, the defaults are emsenn's pools under `--root`:
instances in lib/emsenn/services/board-of-directors/services/executive-office/content/, classes in lib/emsenn/services/board-of-directors/services/executive-office/lib/schemas/.

## When NOT to use

- Not for work already dispatched — this raises; it does not amend.
- Not to record that work is done. Achievement is derived by --verify, and a
  record that could assert its own completion is marking its own homework,
  which is the entire thing the goal exists to prevent.
- Not for standing obligations. If it does not finish, it is a duty, and it
  belongs in the duties pool with tasks raised against it — never here.

Some to hide. Some to listen. From its crest, you can see the clinic on clear days. You can also see who approaches it. No story ends here, but some loop.

Never confirmed.

Services are what some programmers might call "daemons," they're persistent objects that handle persistent engine information. The talker - the thing that handles in-game communication between players - is one service. The socket server that users connect to is another.

The next step of the engine's get-going process is to start, which sends a call to services that will tick. This often does different things - in the case of the MUD socket service, it binds the ports and sets up the server.

It maintains the game tick, which is a loop that, over and over until its told to stop, calls the tick() function in every loaded service, and calls every subscription for which there is an event scheduled. Subscriptions are functions that "happen" the tick after an event related to them are scheduled. For example, a user sending a message through the talker service causes an event to be scheduled, that says basically, "for everyone listening to that channel, show them the message." The next tick, everyone gets shown the message.

From a user perspective, when you connect to the socket server with a MUD client, the game asks you some questions to suss out if you have an existing user account, and creates a new thing, a collection of qualities and their states. For example, all user things have an account ID quality.

The response was not better single predictions, but a different way of listening. Meteorology moved toward ensemble forecasting: running many simulations, each plausible, none authoritative. The question shifted from “what will the weather be?” to “what kinds of weather are now possible?” This was not a retreat from rigor. It was an admission that in a non-stationary system, insisting on a single correct performance is a category error. The musician stops trying to play the piece right and starts trying to stay oriented within a field of possible sounds.

What adapting without stationarity and ergodicity looks like is not Bach played faster. It looks more like jazz, or like communal musics that never relied on a fixed score to begin with. In jazz, there is structure, but it lives in shared constraints rather than scripted outcomes: key centers that can bend, rhythms that can fracture and reassemble, motifs that are offered, taken up, distorted, or dropped entirely. Skill matters—but it is skill at listening, at responding, at leaving space. Mastery is not the ability to reproduce a piece, but to remain musically coherent when the piece dissolves.

The danger is not that people will fail to adapt. The danger is that they will insist on adapting as if the music were still the same, and mistake fidelity for preparedness. Implication only works when the key holds. In a world where the score is dissolving in real time, adaptation becomes less about getting the right notes and more about sustaining the capacity to listen, respond, and remain in relation. Not playing Bach better, but learning how to make music together when there is no longer a piece to return to.

The problem is that this does not only soothe the speaker, it also instructs the listener. Authority ends up doing the work that evidence should be doing.

What is offensive about this is not the presence of fear. Fear is understandable in the face of genuinely difficult systems. What is offensive is the use of elite rhetorical tools to offload that fear onto an audience as certainty. This is pedagogy as displacement, where incomplete understanding is transformed into final-sounding explanation. The speaker gains relief, the listener gains confidence, and the truth is distorted in the process.

About the birds

There’s a little creek behind the apartment. Not much to look at—runs between some chainlink and a parking lot, mostly hidden unless you know to listen for it. I didn’t move here for the view. Moved here for family reasons, and figured I’d be closer to pavement than water for the foreseeable future.

But that creek is there, doing its thing, and the crows have found it.

Most mornings lately, I’ve been seeing them carry bread—sometimes whole slices, sometimes torn hunks—and they drop down to the edge of the creek and dunk it. Not a splash. Just a slow, practiced dip. A few seconds in the water, then they eat.

First time I saw it, I thought maybe it was a one-off. Weird crow behavior. But then I saw it again. And again. So I looked it up.

Turns out, it’s not just a fluke. Crows are known to soak dry or hard food—especially bread—to soften it up. Makes it easier to swallow and digest. Sometimes, it’s even a way of storing food: wet it, wedge it somewhere, come back later. But in this case, it seems like the soaking makes it safer to eat. Bread can swell in a bird’s gut and cause real problems. So this isn’t just clever—it’s adaptive. A behavior learned over time, shared between birds. A practical tradition.

I didn’t expect to live next to a creek again. Growing up, I had creeks nearby in both North Carolina and South Dakota—very different creeks, but both had that mix of quiet and life, of movement just out of sight. I spent hours in and around those waters as a kid. Didn’t think I’d be hearing one from my window again. Certainly not in Duluth.

So here we are. Me, unexpectedly creekside. And the crows, doing what they’ve figured out works.

There’s a lot to admire in that. Crows are sharp, but more than that—they’re socially intelligent. They learn from one another. They remember faces. They respond to changes in their environment, sometimes better than we do. This bread-soaking trick isn’t something every crow just knows. It spreads. It’s culture, in a sense. Crow knowledge, passed down.

That feels meaningful. Not just “neat,” but grounded in something larger. Especially right now.

Because the world is shifting. Climate, sure, but also housing, health, stability—whatever sense we used to have that things moved slowly and predictably. Most folks I talk to are feeling it. And a lot of us are trying to figure out how to keep moving without choking on what we’re handed.

So to see these birds, making do in a changed world—adapting not with panic but with practice—it sticks with me.

They say animals are adjusting just like we are. Guess it’s true.

Nature’s not somewhere else. It’s not just the big parks or deep woods. It’s in the alley behind the apartment. It’s in the birds figuring out how to make dry bread edible, again and again, by running it under the same little stream I walk past on the way to take out the trash.

The crows don’t make a big deal out of it. They just do what works. And if someone’s watching—maybe they learn, too.

Hope they’re not stealing from the bakery.
Though I wouldn’t blame ’em.

by emsenn

I want to start logging what media I engage with, and am curious about the best way to do that with GnoponEmacs. To start, I’m looking at what Org-roam Dailies are like. Checking the Org-roam Manual, it seems like they’re meant for one daily file per day, which isn’t quite what I’m picturing. A separate file for every media log entry seems like it’d cause bloat, but a single file might end up too long. I guess I could chunk them by month or year? But it sounds like for now the right move is to not worry more about it, make org/per/media-log.org, and a capture template at pm for entries, i.e. pmm for music.

And this brings me back to the thing that actually got me hung up and noticed a bug in my slugification function! The question becomes, can I trigger the creation of new notes when being prompted for input on an in-progress capture template? That is, can I go to enter a new music log entry, and then when asked to input the artist, create a new node for that band, using the capture template for that? And the answer is yes. So the next step becomes mapping out which capture templates I would need to smoothly write a music log entry.

Obviously, one for music log entries, that would put a new ID’d subtree under the right timestamp hierarchy, and prompt me for the artist and song/album.

Which brings me to, maybe I need two capture templates: one to record listening to a song, one to record listening to an album… and maybe another for performances? Which would ask for song/album/location respectively… though I guess that doesn’t matter: if we’re triggering sequences of new capture templates, then we can just pick which it is then.

So I need capture templates for:

  • music log entry
  • musician
  • band
  • song
  • album
  • location

All but the first would be entries in my Earth Encyclopedia, at org/ear/enc, and the first would go in org/per/music-log.org.

This will probably quickly cascade to needing more capture templates, but getting that chunk done will be some amount of progress with GnoponEmacs, rather than endlessly planning and abstracting.

Oh, a quick note: I should allow for a Link to the song’s source (usually gonna be YouTube).

And, I should make sure there’s a way for the top songs to make it into the Routine Bulletin I put out? Or at least try and plan on that.

And, I guess thinking more about it, I should aspire to create my own music library, perhaps for running my own pirate online station, but also just to like, be able to play with the library as fluently as I might want. (Music in the MUD?)

Anyway, I want my entries to be entries under a specific day, that’s its own node in the Org-roam database, for example, Music Listening Log, 2025-07-21.

I’ll still need to explore how to render the ID when I’m searching for Org-roam nodes, but other than that, this addresses a lot of the concerns I had about making just, blank-ish nodes.

My next order of consideration is, what information should be considered the first thing that needs to go into a node, and I had the idea earlier that every node can basically describe itself as a form of some other node - assuming we start with a few nodes like acts, conditions, and structures.

This describing thus is the second act of node formation, after titling, and should say the form a thing is derived from, and how it is differentiated.

I’m not quite sure how this grammar maps onto texts like essays - an essay is clear a form of essay, and I guess its content is how it is differentiated from the combination of author, genre, register, and topic that give it form.

Okay, that makes that clear enough. I’m realizing I listed three things - acts, conditions, and structures, but not forms themselves!

There, after all that babbling, I feel like I’ve corrected course toward a more reasonable approach. Currently I have things in subdirectories which just leaves me struggling as to where to put a node, and this gives me a way to make a node whose description is still reasonable, in the language of the system: “This is a node that has been referenced, but not described.”

Which shows us a third act of relating, within the GnoponEmacs system: titling, referencing, and describing. You can’t describe or reference until you’ve titlted, but referencing provides a title in a way that describing doesn’t.

Which highlights that lots of nodes will be created by referencing them, and they’ll likely be referenced as a way of pointing out some form of difference.

Which at this point is just me babbling to affirm the system as reasonable, within its own senses. I’ll have some tweaks to make to the GnoponEmacs code in the morning, starting with creating a template for creating an undescribed node, and then working on the code for publishing.

A note to myself, I want to remember to make sure that Backlinks are attached to published files, but only those Backlinks that are marked, themselves, with a :PUBLISH: tag.

So, “A node is a form of relation differentiated from others by action, condition, or structuration.”

“A music listening log entry is a form of log entry differentiated by focusing on logging music listening log events” is a shitty sentence, but it says what I mean: A /music listening log entry/ is a form of log entry, which is a result of the act of logging (more properly log entering or inputing), but where the input content is music listening events.

Implicit is that logs take log entries, music listening is a form of event, etc. etc., which all needs to get sketched out. A lot of effort, but some of these will get referenced over and over and over - like “event,” which’ll be part of what log event is derived from.

But the benefit will be that I’ll have a node of relations - and how they relate - that’ll be a great foundation for the type of Internet software I want to make - what I call a “MUD” out of habit. I can imagine and speculate what a functional representation of “overcoding” would look like, but it would need to make a lot of assumptions about the system it functioned within. By taking the time to do this coding, I might be able to find a function of overcoding that emerges derivationally from the encoded relations.

Which sounds ambitious, but I remember a time when computers were for doing ambitious things.

And it’s tough because what passes for mutualism in America is so loose and so subsumed within normative power dynamics, that these folk will totally get away with being the climate adaptation leaders of the second half of the decade, because they were the same folk who prevented climate adapting mutualism in the first half.

Just consider, the next time you see some white settler with a job complaining about how hard climate breakdown is making it for them to maintain their consumerist delusions of being engaged with climate adaptation, that they might personally have declined to let someone camp in their lawn to steward a nearby watershed, because “property rights” said it was wrong to do so. Most of all, though, I’m angry because it’s harder than being sad: sad for all the people in the region who don’t wake up with the privilege to choose how they’ll ignore and defer crises that day. It’s hard to not just have sympathy for those who truly can’t make a different move, and let the feelings end there, in a warm and fuzzy sense of compassion.

But they aren’t, and tbh, as someone who is getting older (at least as far as political radicals go), I am ready for young people to start demanding of everyone older than them: “If you know so much about what’s wrong and how it should be better, how come you didn’t do that shit?”

Climate breakdown is not news. Liberalism being fascistic is not news. America being racist and imperialist is not news. They haven’t been news for anyone currently living. Anyone presenting it that way is hiding something, if only their own guilt over their complicity, and you should call them on it.

This is me taking a step toward calling folk on it. I hope the folk who are fretting at young folk about climate breakdown today, so they can advocate for elections and recycling and whatever crap, who ignored me fretting about it 5 years ago, 10 years ago, 15, 20… see this post and realize that while they can lie to Zoomers and Alpha, there are some of of your contemporaries who see how shamefully you’ve used this life you’ve been given, and we’re appalled at the low moral standards you hold yourself to.

Like… there is a lot to unpack there about like, settler-Indigenous relations, leftist relations, there’s just a lot to unpack.

And no one is taking even a passing interest; it seems like it is assumed that if there is anything to care about there, I’ll write about it, connect it to theory, do all that work myself.

Of course, the work will be invalid because it’s coming from someone who was affected by it…

…After all, that’s what happened when I took the time to write back against the academic/institutional narrative of Stop Cop City. Still honestly a bit shook up that someone who called themselves comrade so thoroughly misrepresented things - and more surprised than I’d like to admit that the wider abolitionist field has chosen to completely believe the misrepresentation.

I guess that’s my message:

If you’re young and not white, and reading this, please move forward with a greater confidence in your doubt of settlers. The white worker with the Very Good Sounding Post you just read might be, in another tab, stashing money into their own retirement, while joining a chorus of settlers in a leftist Discord to affirm that liberal organizing is a prerequisite for legitimacy.

Because, as someone who has gotten to see behind the scenes of a lot of leftist scenes… they aren’t much different than the behind-the-scenes at a military base or intelligence conference.

People are playing complex games with their heads and bodies to affirm the liberal way of things as reasonable and legitimate, and they will use whoever they can as a pawn in that, if they can.

It’s not about you, it’s not about us. It’s just about them getting to a place where they can get to sleep without the guilt of their way of life keeping them up, and if climate change has to be a mortal threat to their kids in one breath and something we can manage with a slight shift in the property tax code in the next, then that’s what climate change has to be.

And if something as massive as climate change can be so massively reframed, just to support a feeling, then you better be damn aware that you can, and will, be reframed even more, if it’s necessary to maintain coherence.

Also, just to humanize myself a bit but I have been getting sick every morning for the past 8 mornings, which is a lot for me! I normally struggle with nausea a lot, because of a very bad back injury.

Which is relevant because it is hard to see people talk about “I would integrate things like decolonization into my climate adaptation if I weren’t so busy with a dayjob” as though the working a dayjob isn’t

  1. a need induced by colonization
  2. a privilege afforded by colonization and ability

And it’s frustrating because people so clearly forget that I’m disabled - I’ll write about how folk need to do land work, today, themselves, with their own bodies, and get asked why I’m not doing it myself.

And people also clearly forget that I don’t have my personal documents, due to political repression, so am truly reliant on things like mutualism.

But people don’t like that - they want mutualism to be philanthropy, not mutualism.

So, rather than support me because, y’know, we should do what we can to support other living things, it becomes about supporting me because I produce theory.

But then the theory has to do certain things: make readers feel moral about their own actions, and feel moral about judging the immorality of others actions.

Which is then a form of moral absolution, done through platformized discourse rather than sacred confessional.

And I wouldn’t mind it all so much if the white able-bodied employed settlers who follow me and subscribe to my Ko-Fi were honest with themselves that it has a lot more to do with getting to sleep at night than anything political.

Anyway. I tried to tell folk that the climate situation in North Carolina would be this bad, and was abused for the notion.

Now the crisis is undeniably arriving, and I’m watching the same people who ignored me get ignored by their communities, and get distressed at the contradiction between emergency and lack of response.

And I’m hoping that reading a post like mine might get some of those folk to realize that, rather than keep trying the same things that led them to ignore the warning signs…

…maybe they should go back and actually try and listen to the messages written on the parts of the wall that are now below the waterline.

I guess what I’m working up the nerve to say in this thread is, in my life, I’ve made a lot of choices to do things about the things I’ve seen as problems. Choices to do things that are far outside the window of normal choice.

And I’m trying to have less patience for treating the opinions of folk who have lived their politics through Twitter threads and reading essays on their lunch break as coming from any sort of equivalently informed place.

Not as an appeal to my own authority, but more as a way to… highlight their lack of authority. Because it’s clear that a certain demographic of person is only getting more confident in their ability to solve the world’s problems by engaging with platformized social media just right, and I think that works in part because they can pretend there aren’t people with hands-on experience in the same room.

And that works, in part, because “hands-on” experience is often criminal, or otherwise threatens a person’s living.

It works in part because of how platformized social media works - yes, even the Fediverse.

It works in part because of how liberal ways of knowing work. Yes, even radical ways of knowing.

We’re living in a world where someone who shows up to a months-long political thing for a weekend has more authority over how that political thing is canonized, because that someone has academic credentials, than a person with years-long connections to the things that induced the months-long thing.

And we’re living in a world where people don’t actively appreciate that their sources of truth are so shaped by institutions and such.

It’s a bad spot for anyone trying to figure things out to be in, and I just wish that folk who clearly have nothing figured out didn’t talk so loudly and convincingly at young folk, just to soothe themselves.

Being blunt, I don’t feel like the white settlers and Europeans who read my posts appreciate the risk I take in writing them.

I don’t have citizenship documents. They got destroyed by the government in one of the raids I experienced after Occupy.

For most of the time since this has been a massive inconvience: I can’t get a drivers license, can’t get a job, can’t get food from most food banks, etc.

Under the latest presidency, the risks of not having an ID are changing.

And yet, I continue to bring myself to the same quality of work I was doing before, with the same quality of engagement I was bringing before.

And, on top of that, I continue to publicly share what I learn from that stuff, with an audience that has done more to accidentally dox me than support me, at least in recent times.

Y’all are scared your kids might not have as large of college funds if your boss sees your Fediverse post. I rehearse how to act if ICE raids our house with my family.

Our positionality relative to politics, our political engagement: it might, within the scope of the Fediverse, seem similar. After all, it all boils down to text and maybe some hashtags.

But the perspective that the posts were developed from? Wildly different.

And I think you, white settler radical, are counting on people to not be able to see the difference, so you can use words like mine, combined with the material reinforcement of settler-colonialism, to make sure the world keeps aligning with how you think it should be.

Asshole.

Also I want to be clear that often what I was asking for help for was not like, “Go out and plant corn in your corporate office parking lot,” but like, “Help me with this bit of computer scripting that would auto-forward Associated Press articles mentioning the following cities to the following email address”

The sort of stuff they already do, for money, compartmentalized into nice little bits of work that would actually benefit folk…

But because it wasn’t some moral performance like planting corn in a parking lot, it was largely rejected as any sort of solidarity.

Just, to be clear, I’m not salty because people wouldn’t do spectacular acts of self-sacrifice for my benefit, but because they wouldn’t do anything but that, no matter how much I said it wasn’t benefitting anyone but themselves.

I honestly just would have assumed that as an Indigenous anarchist with on-the-ground experience in Occupy and NES, who writes satirical fantasy tabletop role-playing game materials and LISP code, I would not have found it so difficult to find associates, let alone friends or collaborators, in the Fediverse.

I mean my personal biography almost sounds like what someone would write if they were to make up a fictional mascot for the place!

by emsenn

It’s hard not to get confrontational when I see some folk in North Carolina complaining about how hard the region has been getting hit by climate breakdown recently. There are folk who I am, or used to be, mutuals with, posting about it, and it’s just… hard not to jump in and be like, “Hey, do you regret not putting more effort into organizing against these things earlier, like when I was living in the region, screaming about how the models were underestimating how bad things would get and how quickly?”

Because I was in the region, spearheading guerilla land use projects and trying to agitate political “radicals” toward the same, and it did not work. When I put in requests for specific help to deal with the legal and material consequences of doing guerilla work without an adequate support network, I was ignored, or told that I should have prepared myself better for such consequences, since they’re obvious.

And it’s my fault, for believing that the political rhetoric people used online would relate to how they’d chose to act.

Anyway, it’s tough sitting with like, the names of people I know declined to do anything to help someone organize climate adaptation in a region without any organized climate adaptation and are now trying to step into that organizer role themselves, as though they aren’t responsible for its absence today.

And it’s tough because what passes for mutualism in America is so loose and so subsumed within normative power dynamics, that these folk will totally get away with being the climate adaptation leaders of the second half of the decade, because they were the same folk who prevented climate adapting mutualism in the first half.

Just consider, the next time you see some white settler with a job complaining about how hard climate breakdown is making it for them to maintain their consumerist delusions of being engaged with climate adaptation, that they might personally have declined to let someone camp in their lawn to steward a nearby watershed, because “property rights” said it was wrong to do so. That they might have chosen to go to their dayjob rather than listen to anyone explain how dire the environmental system is. How they continue to go to their dayjob rather than listen to anyone.

Most of all, though, I’m angry because it’s harder than being sad: sad for all the people in the region who don’t wake up with the privilege to choose how they’ll ignore and defer crises that day. It’s hard to not just have sympathy for those who truly can’t make a different move, and let the feelings end there, in a warm and fuzzy sense of compassion.

But that doesn’t give me anything to do. It’s harder to be angry at the people who maybe could do better and simply aren’t. It implies that I have to do something about it, even if that something is just, get a little confrontational with my babblings.

But shit. Someone should. There are a lot of cowards who have been living like cowards their whole lives, and platforms and social norms collaborate to let them seem like the bravest fuckers around.

But they aren’t, and tbh, as someone who is getting older (at least as far as political radicals go), I am ready for young people to start demanding of everyone older than them: “If you know so much about what’s wrong and how it should be better, how come you didn’t do that shit?”

Climate breakdown is not news. Liberalism being fascistic is not news. America being racist and imperialist is not news. They haven’t been news for anyone currently living. Anyone presenting it that way is hiding something, if only their own guilt over their complicity, and you should call them on it.

This is me taking a step toward calling folk on it. I hope the folk who are fretting at young folk about climate breakdown today, so they can advocate for elections and recycling and whatever crap, who ignored me fretting about it 5 years ago, 10 years ago, 15, 20… see this post and realize that while they can lie to Zoomers and Alpha, there are some of your contemporaries who see how shamefully you’ve used this life you’ve been given, and we’re appalled at the low moral standards you hold yourself to.
